length_rule_patches.rule: byte0 low-nibble 9: op-select (byte+2 bits[2:0]) in {0,1} -> length 4
length_rule_patches.why: The op-select field selects the COMPACT 4-byte float form. The old rule fell through to 6 + 2*(byte+4 & 3); for a 4-byte op byte+4 IS THE NEXT INSTRUCTION'S LEADER, and a large share of AGX leaders end in low nibble 7/f (&3==3 -> 12) or 1/5/9/d (&3==1 -> 8). That is the whole mechanism behind falu2_ext8b's 193/250 embedded op-leaders.
length_rule_patches.replacement:
b2 = buf[off + 2] if off + 2 < len(buf) else -1
        if b2 >= 0 and (b2 & 0x07) in (0x00, 0x01):
            return 4                   # EXP-0148 H1: OP-SELECT class rule. byte+2 bits[2:0] is the
                                       # float-ALU op-select; values {0,1} are the COMPACT 4-byte
                                       # accumulate/move class (superset of the enumerated
                                       # 0x18/0x19/0x21/0x30/0x31/0x38/0x39). Must be tested BEFORE
                                       # the 6+2*(byte+4&3) extension, because for a 4-byte op
                                       # byte+4 is the NEXT instruction's leader.
        if b2 in (0x18, 0x38, 0x19, 0x21, 0x31, 0x30, 0x39):
            return 4                   # compact float accumulate/move (arith-enable bit clear).
length_rule_patches.evidence: EXP-0148 corpus A/B (raw/ab/variant_h1_lo9, variant_final4); worked example tessellation__pt_tri_linear__vertex.hex tokenizes end-to-end with zero gaps

length_rule_patches.rule: byte0 low-nibble 9, byte+2 in {0x26,0x2e}: use the uniform 6 + 2*(byte+4 & 3)
length_rule_patches.why: The old `8 if (byte+4 & 0x02) else 6` needed two hand-written special cases above it (byte+4==0x82 -> 10, and the 0x2e/0x87/0x23 signature -> 12). The uniform rule reproduces BOTH (0x82&3==2 -> 10; 0x23&3==3 -> 12) and additionally fixes byte+4==0x81 -> 8.
length_rule_patches.anchor: return 8 if (b4 & 0x02) else 6  # fused mul / mul-add coord op (EXP-0037)
length_rule_patches.replacement:
return 6 + 2 * (b4 & 0x03)  # EXP-0148 H1b: the 0x26/0x2e coord op-selects use the
                                        # SAME byte+4 low-2-bit extension as the rest of the group;
                                        # the old `8 if b4&2 else 6` needed two hand-patches above
                                        # (b4==0x82 -> 10, the 0x2e/0x87/0x23 -> 12) that this rule
                                        # reproduces (0x82&3=2 -> 10, 0x23&3=3 -> 12).

new_value.root_cause: A length rule that reads byte+4 to choose 6/8/10/12 is only sound once the instruction is already known to be at least 6 bytes long. For the compact forms byte+4 belongs to the NEXT instruction, and AGX op leaders overwhelmingly end in low nibble 7/f (&3 == 3 -> 12) or 1/5/9/d (&3 == 1 -> 8). Any future length rule in this ISA must select the form from the LEADING parcel before consulting byte+4.

These six are, by their own committed semantics, NOT hardware opcodes — they are trailing operand / immediate / SFU-coefficient / pad DATA words. Counting them in the emittability denominator is a metric defect: an emitter never emits a pad word, it emits an instruction whose encoding contains those bytes. Recommend excluding them from the emittable-family denominator and marking them host-data rather than untested.
